name: Musée de l'Orangerie
note: The 1852 orangery on the Terrasse du Bord-de-l'Eau: its south front to the Seine glazed (it was a greenhouse), the north to the garden blind with the Rodin bronzes, a door under a pediment on two columns at each end — the west end to the Concorde — and the glass roof over the Nymphéas. Fitted to OSM's 101 × 15 m outline, front SSW to the quai. OSM gives no height (building:levels 3 is the 1965 floors inside the hall): eaves 10 m, the roof's glass top at 13.4.

name: Jeu de Paume
note: The Orangerie's twin (1861) on the Terrasse des Feuillants over the Rue de Rivoli: eighteen round-arched bays a side, glazed to the garden (the front, SSW), blind to Rivoli, the Orangerie's pedimented porch at each end. Fitted to OSM's 82 × 13 m outline.

name: Fondation Louis Vuitton
note: Gehry's twelve glass sails (two tiers, the highest 46 m) over the white Ductal iceberg and its planted terraces, in the Bois de Boulogne. Placed by point and size like the Grand Palais — the plan is drawn in the builder from OSM's way 309626332 (122 × 57 m, centred here), its −z to the south (the Avenue du Mahatma-Gandhi and the basin) — so the frame is the builder's and not one the fit search picks off the blob. OSM's basin round it stays the city's water.

name: Musée du quai Branly
note: Nouvel's pont-musée on its stilts 10 m over Clément's garden, the coloured boxes out of its north face, the louvred south face, the roof restaurant's oval; the Bâtiment Branly's planted wall to the quai, the Auvent and the Université building; the 12 m glass palisade along the quai. Placed by point and size (the outline's 209 × 85 m box, −z to the quai, NNW), the plans drawn in the builder from OSM's outline way 69045431 and its nine building:parts, all named here so they go whether or not the bake superseded the outline. The Palais de l'Alma next door (relation 1084225) is not this museum's.

name: Institut du monde arabe
note: Nouvel's moucharabieh front to the Place Mohammed-V (−z, SW): the steel panels with their irises, 24 × 9 here; the north wing's printed glass curving along the Quai Saint-Bernard to the prow at the west (toward Notre-Dame); the cut and the patio between, open as OSM maps them; the Tour des Livres in the library's glazed west end. Placed by point and size, the plan drawn in the builder from OSM's way 22870791 (77 × 35 m, centred here), because the cut and the patio make the outline concave.

name: Musée Rodin — Hôtel Biron
note: The Hôtel Biron (1732), Rodin's house and museum, between its court on the Rue de Varenne and the sculpture garden: the pale dressed stone of the hôtels particuliers and a slate roof. It needs its own entry — the hôtels' regular expression wants 'Hôtel de/du/des', and OSM names it 'Hôtel Biron'.

name: Musée de Cluny — the Hôtel de Cluny
note: The abbots' Flamboyant Gothic hôtel (c. 1500) and the museum's halls: rough limestone under steep slate, the Marais dress — closer to the late-Gothic house than the hôtels' classical one. OSM maps it as an outline (way 41874779) and eleven building:parts; this claims the parts (the 'Hôtels particuliers' regular expression can only reach the outline's id, which the bake drops when the parts supersede it). The brief's way 56640163 is the museum's site (tourism=museum, no building). If the bake kept the outline instead, the 'Hôtels particuliers' entry (earlier in paris.json, first wins) dresses it classical and this one does nothing.

name: Thermes de Cluny
note: The Gallo-Roman baths' broken walls along the Boulevard Saint-Michel, at OSM's archaeological-site node (Thermes de Cluny): banded rubble and brick, arched openings, the tall wall at the back. Placed by point and size; it replaces the three untagged building:parts of the hôtel's outline that stand there (1132441563/566/567 — the baths' remains as OSM boxes), so the ruins do not stand inside them. The 2018 entrance building (way 1174834795, Desmoulin) stays the city's. −z to the boulevard.

name: Musée Picasso — Hôtel Salé
note: The Hôtel Salé (1659), the Musée national Picasso-Paris, in the Rue de Thorigny: the hôtels' dressed stone and a steep slate roof. OSM leaves the building unnamed (way 57745739, inside the museum's site way 57745741), so the hôtels' regular expression never reached it.

name: Saint-Martin-des-Champs — Musée des Arts et Métiers
note: The priory church, the museum's hall of machines: the church kit's long nave, west gable to the Rue Saint-Martin, the Romanesque choir's apse at the east end, fitted to OSM's outline (75 × 44 m, its ambulatory chapels drawn as the apse). OSM tags it a one-level chapel; 24 m is the nave's ridge. The three building:parts inside its outline (1484904717/718/719) are named too, so they go whether or not the bake superseded the outline.

name: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers
note: The CNAM round the priory — Vaudoyer's and Ancelet's stone fronts to the Rue Saint-Martin and the Rue Réaumur, the cloister and the refectory behind: OSM's multipolygon (182 × 184 m, building:levels 2, which is wrong) in the classical dress at its real four storeys under slate.

name: Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
note: Jules André's gallery of 1889 at the head of the Jardin des Plantes' parterres: the classical stone front to the garden and, over the great nave, the glass roof — a hipped roof in pale glass-grey here. OSM's 8 levels are the galleries inside; the stone walls stand 22 m.

name: Musée Guimet
note: Terrier's museum of 1889 on the Place d'Iéna: the triangular block in the classical dress; its rotunda at the corner on the place is `guimetRotunda`.

name: Musée Guimet — the rotunda
note: The rotunda on the Place d'Iéna: drum, engaged Ionic columns, attic and low dome, standing over the round end of OSM's way 79641993 (restyled above, not replaced). −z to the place (SSW).

name: La Géode
note: Fainsilber's 36 m mirror sphere of steel triangles in its basin before the Cité des Sciences: latitude bands, each quad's two triangles a shade apart so the facets read, sky-pale above and the ground's darker reflection below. Fitted to OSM's round outline (37 m).

name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
note: The old abattoirs' sale hall as Fainsilber rebuilt it: the 280 × 110 m steel-and-glass box, its roof trusses, the planetarium's two domes (OSM's roof parts 251644330/331, claimed here), and the three glass serres on the south-east front facing the Géode. Fitted to OSM's outline, −z to the SE.

name: Philharmonie de Paris
note: Nouvel's shimmering hill of aluminium bird-tiles in six greys over a glazed base, the belvédère's tilted blade at 52 m thrust out over the park, the ramp up the south flank. Fitted to OSM's outline (163 × 104 m, no height in OSM), −z to the park (W). The Cité de la Musique next door (way 63971254) is not claimed.

name: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Tour des Lettres
note: One of Perrault's four L-shaped glass towers (open books on end, 79 m) at the corners of the BnF's esplanade round the sunken garden: glass over the library's wooden shutters, open and shut bay by bay. Fitted to the tower's own OSM outline.

name: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Tour des Temps
note: One of Perrault's four L-shaped glass towers (open books on end, 79 m) at the corners of the BnF's esplanade round the sunken garden: glass over the library's wooden shutters, open and shut bay by bay. Fitted to the tower's own OSM outline.

name: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Tour des Nombres
note: One of Perrault's four L-shaped glass towers (open books on end, 79 m) at the corners of the BnF's esplanade round the sunken garden: glass over the library's wooden shutters, open and shut bay by bay. Fitted to the tower's own OSM outline.

name: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Tour des Lois
note: One of Perrault's four L-shaped glass towers (open books on end, 79 m) at the corners of the BnF's esplanade round the sunken garden: glass over the library's wooden shutters, open and shut bay by bay. Fitted to the tower's own OSM outline.

name: La Sorbonne
note: Nénot's university (1885–1901) between the Rue des Écoles and the Rue Cujas. Placed on OSM relation 572440's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), the main front (−z) to the Rue des Écoles; the plan is the relation's own, with its courts and the notch where the chapel stands. Its parts have no heights and are claimed with it.

name: Chapelle de la Sorbonne
note: Lemercier's domed chapel (1635–42). Placed on OSM way 95860808's box turned to its axis (osmium, 2026-10-30), the west front (−z) to the Place de la Sorbonne, the court's portico to −x.

name: Hôtel-Dieu
note: Gilbert and Diet's hospital (1866–78) on the north side of the Parvis de Notre-Dame. Placed on OSM relation 2449758's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), the front (−z) to the Parvis; the plan is the relation's own, the ward pavilions and courts, with its parts and the small hospital block in the first court (relation 11598195) claimed with it. Cornice from memory: OSM's parts (9–15 m) read low.

name: Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève
note: Labrouste's reading room (1843–51) on the north side of the Place du Panthéon. Placed on OSM way 55353486's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), the arcaded front (−z) to the Place; nineteen arched bays over the lettered panels, the proportions from a Mapillary frame along it; the wings behind are the rest of the way.

name: École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts
note: Duban's exhibition building (1858–62) and the Hôtel de Chimay on the Quai Malaquais. Placed on OSM relation 969872's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), the arched front (−z) to the quai. The Palais des Études behind it, relation 3856419, is not this model.

name: Hôpital Saint-Louis — the Quadrilatère
note: Vellefaux's quadrangle (1607–12) of brick, stone and slate. Placed on OSM relation 10714749's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), the gate pavilion (−z) to the Rue Bichat side; the eight pavilions and four ranges from the ring. Its parts, all under the ranges, are claimed with it.

name: La Salpêtrière — the main front
note: Le Vau, Le Muet and Bruant's long range (1656–77) across the head of its garden, now the Pitié-Salpêtrière. Placed on OSM's Divisions Mazarin and Lassay and the gateway between them (osmium, 2026-10-30), with their parts, the front (−z) down the garden to the Boulevard de l'Hôpital. The chapel behind is not this model and is not claimed.

name: Les Docks — Cité de la Mode et du Design
note: Jakob + MacFarlane's lime-green tube (2008–12) over the 1907 concrete warehouses of the Magasins généraux, on the Quai d'Austerlitz. Placed on OSM way 78535563's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), the tube's side (−z) to the Seine.

name: Rotonde de la Villette
note: Ledoux's customs barrier (1784–88), a drum on a cube, on the Place de Stalingrad. Placed on OSM way 63971487's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30); one of the four porticos (−z) to the Place.

name: Pavillon de l'Arsenal
note: Bruyerre's brick and iron exhibition pavilion (1878–79), the city's architecture centre, on the Boulevard Morland. Placed on OSM way 56186898's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), the front (−z) to the boulevard, confirmed as the side the boulevard runs by OSM's street geometry; dressing from memory.

name: Collège de France
note: Chalgrin's court (1774–80) open to the Rue des Écoles, with the later wings beside and behind it. Placed on OSM's three blocks' box (osmium, 2026-10-30), the court's mouth (−z) to the Rue des Écoles; plans are OSM's, the dressing from memory.

name: Tour Zamansky
note: Albert's Jussieu tower (1971, reclad by 2009). OSM way 16924888: 23.4 m square, 90 m, 29 levels. Dressing from memory.

name: La Pagode
note: Marcel's Japanese hall (1896), a cinema since 1931, on the Rue de Babylone. Placed on OSM way 68739427's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30). Roofs and porch from memory.

name: Mairie du 5e arrondissement
note: Guénepin's mairie (1844–50), the twin of Soufflot's École de Droit across the Rue Soufflot, on the Place du Panthéon. Placed on OSM relation 660657's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30); the frontispiece is on the outline's diagonal, facing the Panthéon, between local −z and +x.

name: Ancienne Mairie du 1er and the belfry
note: Hittorff's mairie (1855–60, now Quartier Jeunes) and Ballu's belfry (1858–62) on the Place du Louvre, beside Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois (its own entry). Placed on OSM's two outlines' box (osmium, 2026-10-30), the front (−z) to the Colonnade.

name: Piscine Joséphine-Baker
note: The floating pool (2006) on the Seine at the Quai François-Mauriac. On OSM way 119943935's box. Its hull goes down to the model's base, the river bed: its freeboard depends on the Seine's level, unchecked.

name: Le Zénith
note: Chaix and Morel's tent (1983) at La Villette, on OSM way 63971432's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), 20 m as tagged. Ribs and mast from memory.

name: Musée Jacquemart-André
note: Parent's private palace (1869–75) on the Boulevard Haussmann. Placed on OSM way 68804399's box turned to its walls (osmium, 2026-10-30), its straight side (−z) to the boulevard and the court OSM cuts out of the north behind it. Which side the cour d'honneur's ramps stand on could not be confirmed; the dressing is from memory.
